Chapter 1

Introduction

1.1Nivôse under the ice

Nivôse is an island in the far north, locked in the pack ice. Fifteen hamlets survive there thanks to eight geothermal drill rigs that keep them warm. One winter morning, the Concession, the company of Prefect Anselm Krag, lands at the Bastion to seize the rigs. Its columns of armored vehicles leave the Bastion at dawn; its garrisons hold the fuel depot, the tank plant and the radio relay.

You command the Hamlet Guard, a militia of mountain folk, hunters, doctors and pilots. At first, the Guard is you and a handful of loyal friends. Everyone else must be won over, hamlet after hamlet, by earning the trust of people who each have their own friendships and grudges. Then you must hold the rigs, cut the roads, sabotage, ambush, and survive the cold.

1.2Two ways to play, one war

Guérilla is played at two scales, which make up a single campaign:

  • The command map, turn by turn. Each recruit has two hours per turn to travel, recruit, resupply, sabotage or fight. When everyone has acted, you synchronize watches and the Concession moves.
  • The 3D view, in real time, in first person or isometric view. You take control of a recruit: skiing, shooting, snowmobile, hang glider, aircraft, belfry… Everything that happens there counts for the campaign.

Guérilla is a free remake of Midwinter (Mike Singleton, 1989). The island, characters and story are original. In Old Norse, Vetrarhríð means both “winter storm” and “winter assault”.

Chapter 2

The aim of the game

2.1Drive out the Concession

Your aim is to drive the Concession out of Nivôse. There are two ways to do it: blow up the Bastion, its headquarters, or destroy the tank plant and then every column still on the move.

Neither happens in one stroke. The Bastion is held by fourteen soldiers, the plant by eight, and every column rolls with its tanks. You must first grow, then weaken the Concession, then strike.

2.2The stages of a campaign

  1. Recruit. Thirty-two islanders can join the Guard (forty-two on Premium islands). Each one only follows certain people: read their files.
  2. Hold the rigs. A hamlet that loses its rig goes cold: it resupplies badly, its people rest badly, its trust erodes. If the Concession holds every rig, the game is lost.
  3. Weaken the Concession. Sabotage the fuel depot (columns run short of fuel) and the radio relay (columns lose their way, mortars lose their spotter), blow the bridges over the gorge, cut the telegraph.
  4. Strike. Rout columns by destroying their command vehicle, free occupied hamlets, then attack the plant or the Bastion.

At the end, the epilogue tells the story of the war you fought (how you fought matters as much as the outcome) and gives it a score.

Chapter 3

Victory and defeat

3.1Winning

You win as soon as:

  • the Bastion is destroyed;
  • or the tank plant is destroyed and every Concession column has been routed or has withdrawn.

A map made in the editor (Premium) can set a different objective, shown in the game's introduction and in the menu:

ObjectiveVictoryDefeat
Hold drill rigs until a given dayhold at least N rigs until the end of day Dfewer than N rigs held
Destroy Concession installationsall the chosen installations are destroyed—
Free occupied hamletsall the chosen hamlets (or all hamlets) belong to the Guard—
Keep the commander free until a given daythe commander is still free at the end of day Dthe commander dies or is captured

Such maps can also set a time limit: once the last day has passed, the game is lost.

3.2Losing

Whatever the objective, you lose if:

  • the Concession holds every drill rig: without heat, the hamlets surrender one after another;
  • no one is left in the Guard: no active recruit, and no imprisoned recruit who could still be freed.
A captured recruit is not lost. When taken out of the fight, they are locked up in the guard post of the nearest Concession-held hamlet, or at the Bastion. They can escape, or their comrades can come and free them (see Fighting).

3.3The score

When the game ends, the epilogue tells the story of your war, then the score adds it all up:

What countsPoints
Bastion destroyed+1,000
Concession exhausted (plant and columns) or objective achieved+900
Speed (if you win)+600, minus 60 per day after the first
Each drill rig held+60
Average trust of the hamlets×4
Each Guard member still standing+25
Each vehicle destroyed+10
Each column routed+40
Each act of sabotage+30
Each bridge down · each telegraph line cut+20 · +10
Each aircraft shot down+30
Each Guard member killed−80
Each islander killed by the Guard−150

The total is multiplied according to the winter's severity (×0.8 on Mild, ×1 on Harsh, ×1.3 on Severe, ×1.6 on Deadly), then you receive a title: Survivor, Mentioned in Guard Dispatches (900), Great Cold Medal (1,700), Cross of the Hamlets (2,600) or Hero of Nivôse (3,600).

Chapter 4

Difficulty levels

4.1The severity of winter

On the title screen, the Severity of the winter row offers four levels. Hover over a button (or select it with a controller): a tooltip sums up what it changes.

MildHarshSevereDeadly
For whomfor learningthe reference wintera hard winterno mercy
Columns at the start2344
Tanks per column1234
New columnevery 16 daylight hoursevery 12 daylight hoursevery 8 daylight hoursevery 8 daylight hours
Column speed−10%normal+12%+12%
Soldiers' spotting−20%normal+20%+20%
Soldiers' accuracy−20%normal×1.5×1.5
Air threats by defaultnoneaircraft-guided mortarsmortars and fightermortars and fighter
Advanced campaign ★Krag reacts slowly; sweeps of 4 men, no dogssweeps of 5 men, with dogsKrag reacts fast; elites and Krag's hunterssame, plus the scarlet column
Score×0.8×1×1.3×1.6

Deadly uses all the rules of Severe, but wounds are unforgiving: a soldier or dog that is hit dies; your recruit, when hit, is pinned down; a squadmate falls at the first bullet and dies at the second. In towns, armed passers-by report you, and stealing a car raises the alarm.

On the other levels, a squadmate goes down after a number of hits equal to half their endurance (rounded up), and dies after as many hits as their endurance.

4.2Game options

Below the severity row, a few buttons switch on or off. Choosing a severity sets the air threats first; you can then change them.

Aircraft-guided mortars
An observation aircraft directs the mortars of nearby columns.
Attack fighter
A fighter hunts the Guard with rockets from 8:00 to 16:00.
Fog of war
On the map, you only see what your recruits and friendly hamlets spot.
Guided first mission
A guide walks you through your first steps. Recommended for a first game.
Advanced campaign ★
Krag's general staff responds to your strikes (Premium, on by default; see Advanced campaign).

4.3The daily challenge

The Daily challenge button starts the same game for everyone that day: same island, same weather, same random events, on Harsh, with guided mortars, no fighter and no advanced campaign. Compare your scores. Premium adds the island of the day, a random island shared by all.

Chapter 5

The free game

5.1What the free game includes

The base game is free and complete: the whole Nivôse campaign can be played without buying anything.

  • The island of Nivôse: 40 km across, fifteen hamlets, eight drill rigs, four Concession installations, the Brisante gorge, three cable cars, four airstrips.
  • 32 recruits, each with a home hamlet, skills, a story and ties to others.
  • The four levels of winter severity, the options and the guided first mission.
  • The daily challenge.
  • The game in English or French, your choice.
  • The command map and the 3D view: first person, isometric view, behind the commander.
  • Skiing, walking, snowmobile, towing, hang glider, cable car, aircraft; seven weapons, grenades and charges.
  • Weather, night, cold, hunger, avalanches, thin ice, tracks, trackers and dogs.
  • Campaign events, epilogues and score.

5.2The title screen

Who commands the Guard? Choose A male commander (Erwan Kerlann, selected at launch) or A female commander (Maëlle Kerlann). First and last names can be changed in the two fields. Below the two portraits, four color swatches set their appearance: only skin and hair change, nothing in the rules.

Next come the severity of the winter, the options, then the world: Nivôse, or the Premium worlds (★). A thumbnail shows the shape of the chosen island before you start. The Language row offers Automatic (the system language), Français or English; you can also switch language during a game, from the menu. The buttons at the bottom start a new game or the daily challenge, let you continue your last game, load or import another, and open the manual (How to play) and the ★ Premium window.

5.3The command map

Time. Each turn lasts two hours for every member of the Guard. Play them one after another: the map shows the columns at the selected recruit's time. When everyone has acted, press Synchronize watches: the Concession takes its turn and the log reports what happened.

On the left, the Guard: active recruits (with their remaining time), those to recruit and their hamlet, the prisoners and the fallen. On the right, the selected recruit's file: skills, weapons, wounds, food, fatigue, morale, cold, and available actions. At the top, the time, day and turn, the weather and forecast, avalanche risk, the state of the eight rigs, and the menu.

The map has a legend: drill rigs, hamlets, mountain huts, enemy columns and installations, isolated buildings, airstrips, aircraft, cable cars, tracks and trackers. Tap a place for its card and route.

5.4Moving around

Select a recruit, tap a point on the map or a hamlet: the route appears with its duration. Press Go. A journey too long for one turn can carry on by itself: Go and continue on later turns.

On skis, travel times are those of a loaded skier in snow, following the alpine clubs' method: an average recruit covers about 5 km/h on the flat, climbs 250 to 370 m per hour and descends much faster than they climb. Crossing Nivôse takes a good day. A good skier goes faster; fatigue, leg wounds, night, fresh snow and storms slow you down. The Concession moves at the same pace: its columns advance in stages, with halts.

By snowmobile, you race along at over 30 km/h on the flat, but you can be heard from afar, you burn fuel (refuel at a hamlet garage) and you get cold fast. Skiers in the same group can be towed.

Cable cars link Hautbrume, Pierrefonte and Port-Lys to the mountain huts; ride up in the cabin and come down by hang glider: Take a hang glider at the hut, then Take off and choose where to land (in 3D: Take off by hang glider). A line stops if its hamlet falls. The hang glider cannot take off in strong wind.

Aircraft. Two Concession liaison planes wait at the Brisants airfield. The commander, or a recruit who can fly (Flying 4 or more), can steal them: you can only take off and land on a groomed strip (the Brisants, the Plateau, the Fumerolles, the Banquise). On the map, a Guard aircraft flies from strip to strip in a few minutes; next to a parked plane, Take the controls opens the 3D view in the cockpit. Every plane carries a parachute: you can bail out in flight and land anywhere, even on a roof. Near an airstrip, the autopilot can do the landing. About a thousand meters above the highest summit, the plane stalls: that is its ceiling.

Standing orders are given in a recruit's file: Go and continue for a long journey, Guard a hamlet (resupply, heal, organize its defense and fight when a column arrives), Rest until healed. They play out on their own at synchronization, or at once with Run orders at the top of the Guard list.

5.5Recruiting and winning over hamlets

Recruiting. Each islander only follows certain people. Read the files: a brother, a fiancée, an old friend open doors; a grudge closes them. A persuasive recruit convinces better.

Hamlet trust. Every strike near a hamlet may bring a reprisal raid, and fear sets in. A distrustful hamlet ends up denouncing recruits who stop there; a trusting hamlet reports nearby columns and patrols and is more willing to follow you. Freeing a hamlet restores its trust; killing an islander ruins it.

Morale gives a steady hand and a convincing voice. A church, a hot meal, a successful sabotage raise it; hunger and cold wear it down.

Rigs and heat. Each hamlet is connected to a drill rig. While the Guard holds it, people eat and sleep warm and trust grows. If the rig is lost, the hamlet goes cold: a snowflake marks it on the map.

5.6Fighting

Columns. A column has one to four tanks depending on the severity; it spots nearby recruits. Engage it in quick resolve from the map, or take control in 3D. Destroying its command vehicle, circled in white, routs it. When a column spots you in 3D, a tank may leave the road to hunt you down and fire its heavy shells.

Armor. Bullets do nothing against a tank. You need the bazooka, taken from the armory of a depot, a plant or the Bastion (one rocket, one vehicle), or two grenades: the first sets the vehicle smoking, the second destroys it.

Weapons. Everyone sets off with a knife, a 9 mm pistol and their favorite weapon:

WeaponIn short
KnifeKills silently from behind; it can be thrown (right click), then picked up.
9 mm pistolThe backup weapon, usable on a snowmobile.
Submachine gunShort bursts at close range, usable on a snowmobile.
Assault rifleSingle shots or bursts, at medium range.
Shotgun (pump-action)Five shells, deadly up close, usable on a snowmobile.
Scoped riflePrecision fire at long range; pierces aircraft, but useless against armor.
BazookaOne rocket per shot, three at most; with grenades, the only weapon against tanks.

An armory lets you change weapons and resupply: Take or Leave a weapon, two long arms at most. Charges are taken from a workshop; grenades are thrown.

Garrisons. Occupied hamlets and installations are held by infantry (four per hamlet, six at the depot, four at the relay, eight at the plant, fourteen at the Bastion). Kill a hamlet's whole garrison and it is freed; an installation's, and its turrets fall silent.

Prison and escape. A recruit taken out of the fight is locked up in the guard post of the nearest held hamlet (otherwise at the Bastion), and their weapons are confiscated there. Six hours later, they can try to escape from their file (one failure means a twelve-hour wait): they come out with their skis and a knife. Their comrades can also storm the post from the map, or kill the garrison in 3D.

Friendly fire. A Guard recruit hit by your bullets cries out and runs for cover; hit again, they fire back. Once down, one more shot finishes them. Those who turned their weapon on you desert.

5.7Sabotage and buildings

Sabotage. Take charges from a workshop. The depot, plant and relay weaken the Concession; a guard post frees a hamlet and its prisoners. In 3D, plant the charge against the wall with F. Once sabotaged, the depot and the plant burn for hours and can be seen from very far away. Whatever is destroyed stays in ruins.

Buildings. In 3D, walk up to a door and press F; the hamlet menu (on the map and in 3D) also groups their actions.

  • House and cabin: hot meal, a warm night.
  • Church and chapel: the first visit restores morale; Climb the belfry opens the 3D view at the top of the church, to shoot from above while staying hidden.
  • Bunker: covered firing post and shelter.
  • Shop: food, ammunition, a few charges. Garage: refuelling and rearming.
  • Radio station: call up to four islanders from afar, once the relay's jamming is lifted.
  • The Concession's powder magazine, warehouse, workshop, synthesis plant and radio station can be sabotaged with charges: scarce ammunition, delayed reinforcements, columns short of fuel.

The telegraph. Concession posts alert each other by wire: a fire spotted, a post attacked, and the neighbors send men. At the foot of a pole, F cuts the line: the post is isolated until a repair crew arrives, which you can ambush.

The Brisante gorge. A canyon cuts the island between the Bastion and the north. Columns cross it by two bridges: a charge planted at an abutment brings them down, along with any vehicles on them. Without a bridge, columns make detours of dozens of kilometers.

5.8Surviving the winter

Cold. Outdoors, the body cools: faster at night, in strong wind, when still or on a snowmobile; effort warms you. Chilled, you aim badly and tire; with hypothermia, you get hurt. A hamlet or a mountain hut warms you up. Elsewhere, bivouac on the map, or light a campfire in 3D.

Hunger. You get hungry on the move, more so when exerting yourself: eat a ration (a hamlet serves a hot meal and gives you more). On an empty stomach, you tire and the cold bites faster. In severe cold, aiming, shooting and reloading bare-handed freeze your fingers: frostbite makes your aim shake; a fire or a medic heals it.

Skis. The wax must match the snow: blue in hard frost, violet around −8 °C, klister when the snow turns. It wears off over the kilometers: re-wax in a hamlet. Climbing skins let you climb straight up a slope (they brake when going down). A fall can break a binding, which you mend with wire. On foot, you can climb slopes too steep for skis.

Snow shelter. Standing still on an open slope, you dig a trench shelter: inside, the cold barely bites and you are hard to see from afar. On the map, the bivouac digs one too.

Fires. A fire warms you quickly, but it can be seen: at night its glow carries 4 to 5 km under a clear sky; by day, it's the smoke. A sentry who spots it sends trackers.

The weather changes on its own: clear, hazy, overcast, snow, storm, freezing fog. Snow and storms slow you down, reduce visibility (you are spotted less) and ground the aircraft.

At night, from 18:00 to 6:00, the columns bivouac. You see less and are seen less: it's the hour for sabotage. But headlights, searchlights and flares pierce the dark.

Avalanches. After heavy snowfall, the risk rises (shown at the top of the screen). A grenade, a rocket or a charge on a steep slope can release a slab that buries everything in its path, columns included.

Ice. Lakes and pack ice hold, except where the ice stays dark and thin: it sings, cracks, then gives way. Fall in and you come out soaked: find a fire, fast.

5.9Seeing without being seen

Tracks. Your skis and snowmobiles leave tracks, visible on the map. A garrison that finds fresh ones sends trackers who follow them all the way to you. Snow and wind erase them; in a Guard hamlet, trackers give up.

Dogs. Trackers have shepherd dogs. The wind carries your scent: downwind, a dog smells you from several hundred meters.

Binoculars zoom from ×2 to ×16 and switch to night vision, then thermal (which drains the batteries). The rangefinder gives the distance; keep a target in the reticle to mark it on the minimap. They also show the slope and the avalanche risk.

Being seen. Buildings, rocks and terrain hide you; crouching or lying still, you are less visible.

Enemy aircraft. Depending on the options, an observation plane directs the mortars and a fighter hunts the Guard by day. They can be shot down; destroying the relay cuts the mortars, the depot reduces sorties.

5.10The squad and events

The squad. Recruits at the same place go with you in 3D. Give them an order (follow me, hold position, flank the enemy) and a fire discipline (fire at will or hold fire). A downed comrade can be carried on your shoulder. Behind your snowmobile, skiers get towed.

Events. From time to time, after a synchronization, the island forces a choice on you: a deserter to question, a hamlet calling for help (promise, and keep your word), a great storm on the way, a convoy to surprise, a child lost in the night, an offer of medical help…

5.11The 3D view and the isometric view

From a recruit's file, Switch to 3D view opens the first-person view. Y switches to the isometric view: the camera hovers over the recruit as over a strategy table; click the ground to move, click an enemy to shoot, and you only see what the recruit sees. In isometric view, B puts the camera behind the commander. In a car, the same Y key gives the rear view.

Fast time (T) makes time pass four times faster: travel, but also enemies, cold, hunger, fire and tasks.

Saving. The game saves itself at every important step, every five minutes in 3D and when you quit. Continue resumes it; Load… opens the other slots.

Chapter 6

The Premium version

6.1What Premium adds

Premium opens every island and gives the Concession a real mastermind. On Steam, it is the “Guérilla — Premium” DLC; outside Steam, a license key to paste into the ★ Premium window on the title screen. Premium features carry a star ★.

FeatureIn short
Random islandNew terrain and a random start, 40, 10 or 5 km across.
Island of the dayThe same random island and the same rules for everyone, every day.
Real mapAny place in the world, from free OpenStreetMap data; whole towns with their passers-by and cars.
Advanced campaignKrag's general staff answers every blow you strike.
Ten more partisans42 recruits instead of 32, outside Nivôse and the island of the day.
EditorRework an island, write a scenario, choose your starting recruits.
My mapsKeep, export and share your maps.
Stream DeckThe “Guérilla Deck” plugin shows the game's state and controls it.

6.2The random island

The Random island ★ button draws a brand-new island: terrain, hamlets, installations and the commander's starting point. Its number (the seed) identifies it: the same seed gives the same island; Draw another island offers a new one. Below the world row, the Island size row offers 40 km (the whole island), 10 km (about 8 hamlets, a shorter game) or 5 km (about 4 hamlets, a short game). A small island has fewer columns, patrols and recruits, but all five installations remain.

6.3The island of the day

The Island of the day ★ link draws the same random island for every player that day, with the daily challenge's rules. It stays at 40 km and keeps 32 recruits, so that everyone plays on equal terms.

6.4The real map

Type a place (a town, a summit, a valley: Chamonix, Mont Ventoux, Lofoten…) or coordinates. The game downloads the terrain (Terrain Tiles) and the villages with their real buildings, roads, rivers, lakes, forests, airfields and bridges (OpenStreetMap). Choose the scale: 20 km (stretched terrain: a valley, a small island), 40 km (true scale) or 60 km (compressed terrain: a whole range).

Every real building is there and stops skiers and vehicles; the church, chapels, shops, garages, police station and mountain huts work like those of Nivôse. Columns drive faster on main roads and cross rivers by the bridges.

City maps (City 5 km or City 10 km, in the real place window) load every building in the central square. The game places no hamlet or installation there: you place them in the editor (or let the game place what's missing at random). The streets come alive: passers-by, parked cars and traffic. You can take a car (F by the door): 90 km/h on roads, 40 on tracks, 12 in snow; an exploding car acts like a grenade. The town's famous monuments are modeled and can be seen through binoculars.

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL license). A city map can take several minutes to download.

6.5The advanced campaign

With the Advanced campaign ★ box ticked (on by default with Premium), the Concession learns from your strikes:

  • strike the same sector often, and a sweep company will comb it, then follow any fresh tracks it finds;
  • ambush often, and columns will roll escorted by infantry;
  • approach an installation, and its garrison will be reinforced and put on alert (doubled sentries, harder sabotage); a threatened Bastion keeps a column in reserve;
  • free a hamlet, and the nearest column will come to retake it;
  • on Severe and Deadly, the Concession's elites (red uniforms, better shots) come into play: Krag's hunters on your trail, the Bastion garrison, the command vehicle's crew; on Deadly, the scarlet column when the Guard holds half the rigs;
  • Krag may post an ultimatum in the hamlets.

The synchronization report sums up what is known of his intentions, much more with radio interception. Without the advanced campaign (free game, daily challenge and island of the day), the Concession keeps its columns, garrisons and aircraft, but does not react to your strikes.

6.6Ten more partisans

On random islands, real maps and editor maps, ten more islanders can join the Guard, for 42 recruits in all. Each has a home hamlet, a story, friendships and grudges, and a part in the island's events.

6.7My maps

My maps ★ keeps your creations. Export a map as a .carte-guerilla.json file for another player, who imports it in the same place. Saved games remember their map.

6.8The Stream Deck

With the Guérilla Deck plugin installed in the Stream Deck software, the game connects by itself: the keys show your weapon and ammunition, binoculars, what you can do here, the time and time left, heading, body, recruit and rigs, and send some fifty commands to the game. A “Stream Deck connected” message confirms it.

Chapter 7

The editor

7.1Opening the editor

The editor (Premium) prepares a game before you play it: rework an island, write a scenario, choose the recruits. Open it with the Editor ★ button on the title screen.

The right-hand panel shows the starting map. Start from another map offers Nivôse, a random island (40, 10 or 5 km), a real place (name or coordinates) or a map from My maps. Changing map discards unsaved edits.

7.2The tools

ToolWhat it does
Move, adjustDrag a hamlet, installation, mountain hut, airstrip, added building or patrol waypoint. Tap it without moving it to open its settings. The terrain is leveled around the new spot when the game starts.
Add a hamletTap the map to found a hamlet: it gets its houses, its guard post and the equipment you give it.
Add a buildingPick a type, then tap the map. The door direction turns in 15° steps, or at random. The powder magazine, warehouse, workshop and plant belong to the Concession.
Post a patrolTap the first waypoint of the round, then the next ones (eight at most); tap the last or the first again to close the round. A single point makes a fixed post. Set the number of soldiers, the dog, and the schedule (always, by day, by night).
Commander's startTap where the commander begins the game.
Remove or restoreTap a hamlet, building, addition, patrol or the start. Tap it again to restore it.
Test here in 3DTap the map: the commander drops into 3D there, on the map as you have edited it. Esc, then “Back to the editor”.
+ Add a monumentOn a city map: tap a building to turn it into a monument, or an empty spot for a statue, a lighthouse or a tower.

The selected place shows its settings: name, equipment (snowmobiles in the garage, hang gliders), door direction, a patrol's soldiers and round. A removed hamlet sends its people to the nearest hamlet; for a mountain hut, only the name can change.

7.3The scenario

The Scenario panel says what the map imposes on the game. Left empty, a setting follows the title screen and the difficulty.

Title and briefing
The briefing is shown at the start of the game; each line break starts a paragraph.
Difficulty, aircraft, fog of war
Imposed, or left to the player.
Start time, weather for the first six hours
Clear, overcast, snow, storm, fog, or natural weather.
Columns
Columns at the start, vehicles per column (1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8), reinforcements, columns at once, the columns' first targets (in order).
Hamlets occupied at the start
They start with a garrison; their people are prisoners.
Objective and time limit
Standard, hold rigs until a given day, destroy installations, free hamlets, keep the commander free (see Victory and defeat).
Recruits
Tap a recruit to change their state: to recruit → in the Guard (starting recruit) → absent. All 42 recruits are offered; on a reworked Nivôse, the ten Premium recruits are absent by default.

7.4Recruit skills

Each recruit has eight skills, from 0 to 10: Skiing, Shooting, Driving, Flying, Explosives, Endurance, Medicine, Persuasion. In the editor, each can gain or lose two points at most; a point added is taken from another skill of the same recruit, and vice versa. Original values undoes a recruit's edits.

7.5Checking, saving, starting

Checks flags whatever would prevent play (hamlets, rigs, airstrips, start, objective); show points to the spot on the map. ↶ Undo and ↷ Redo step through every edit (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z; Cmd on Mac).

In This map, give a name and an author, then Save to My maps or Export (file). Start the game plays the map; Clear all starts from scratch; Quit returns to the title screen.

City maps. The To place panel lists the hamlets, huts and installations to place before playing; Place what's missing at random places them for you. The Monuments panel shows, removes or adds monuments and sets their type and height.

Chapter 8

Controls

8.1Before you start

Keys are given for a QWERTY keyboard. The game follows the position of the movement keys: on an AZERTY keyboard, you move forward with Z, go left with Q, lean left with A, and the distress flare is on W. The other letters (F, R, J…) are the same on both keyboards. The in-game manual (How to play) shows the keys of your own keyboard.

A controller works in the 3D view; its buttons are also listed on the pause screen. The map can be used by touch as well as with the mouse.

8.2On the command map

ClickSelect a recruit, a place, a destination; open a card.
EnterGo to the chosen destination.
EscCancel the route, close a window.
NNext recruit.
3Switch to 3D view with the selected recruit.
+ − ◎Zoom in, zoom out, recenter the map (buttons at bottom right); the mouse wheel zooms too.

8.3Moving in 3D

On skis, the slope carries you. W pushes on the poles; S snowplows (at speed, S turns the skis sideways: a skid to a stop); A and D turn; Shift tucks for speed; Space jumps. Across a slope you slide downhill; a good skier holds their edges. Your weapon goes on your back as you speed along and comes back as soon as you aim.

On foot (I takes your skis off or puts them back on, a few seconds, standing still): W S to walk forward and back, A D to sidestep, Shift to run. It is slow in powder, but you can climb slopes too steep for skis and slip between houses.

Positions: C goes down one step (standing, crouching, prone), Space gets you up. Prone, you can't move, but your weapon is rested: your aim barely sways and you are harder to see.

Skis: P puts climbing skins on or off; U fixes a binding with wire.

Looking follows the mouse; the arrow keys turn your head too. Holding Q or E leans left or right to look and shoot from behind a tree, a rock or a corner. T toggles fast time (×4).

8.4Fighting in 3D

Left clickFire (with binoculars: mark the target).
Right clickAim; with the knife, throw it.
1 … 6Choose a weapon; 7: the bazooka.
WheelChange weapon; with binoculars, zoom.
RReload.
BFire mode (single shot, burst).
VKnife strike.
GThrow a grenade.
ZDistress flare, when the recruit can no longer move (also F): islanders come to fetch them and the 3D view closes.

8.5Acting, observing, surviving

FInteract: open a door, talk to an islander, open the hamlet menu, get in or out of a vehicle, carry a downed comrade, plant a charge, cut a telegraph line, steal an aircraft.
JBinoculars. N or right click: night vision, then thermal. Wheel, + and −: zoom.
XEat a ration.
KDig a snow shelter (standing still, on an open slope).
HLight a campfire; next to the flames, smother it with snow.
OSquad order: follow me, hold position, flank the enemy.
LFire discipline: fire at will or hold fire (at the controls of a plane: automatic landing).
YFirst-person view ↔ isometric view.
M or TabBack to the map (not in flight or in a cabin).
EscPause.

8.6The isometric view

Click the groundMove there; W A S D take back control.
Click an enemyFire; the recruit aims from the shoulder.
Arrows · WheelTurn the camera by quarter turns, zoom.
BCamera behind the commander, or free camera.
GThrow a grenade towards the pointed spot.
VAim at the enemy under the cursor, close by.

8.7Vehicles

Snowmobile. W accelerates, S brakes, A and D turn. The mouse turns your head while the vehicle keeps its course; your head returns to center when you let go of the mouse. On a snowmobile, only the pistol, submachine gun and pump-action shotgun can be used.

Towing. Behind a comrade's snowmobile, press F next to them to be towed; W faster, S slower, A/D to show the direction, F to let go of the rope.

Car (city maps). F by the door to get in; W accelerates, S brakes and reverses, A/D steer; F when stopped to get out. Y gives the rear view.

Hang glider. W dives, S pulls up, A/D bank; the mouse turns your head. Drill rigs create thermals.

Aircraft, cockpit view. W/S set the throttle; A/D or ← → bank; ↑ pulls up, ↓ dives; Space brakes on the ground; the mouse turns your head. Below 100 km/h the aircraft stalls: land along the strip, wings level, without diving.

Aircraft, exterior view (Y). W/S climb and dive, A/D bank, holding the left or right mouse button (or Shift/Ctrl) opens or closes the throttle, Space brakes; holding ← → turns the camera, ↑ ↓ zoom; dragging the mouse with a button held also turns the camera. Off the strip, on the ground, the aircraft taxis slowly through the snow.

Autopilot. Within 3 km of an airstrip, L starts the automatic landing; L again disengages it. It gives up if terrain blocks the approach, the strip has been overshot or fuel runs out: then take back the controls.

Parachute. In flight, press F, then F again within two seconds: you bail out and the plane flies on without a pilot. In free fall, Space opens the canopy (“Open!” appears as the ground gets close); A/D turn, W/S move forward or back. Under the canopy, A/D turn, W speeds up, S brakes: just before the ground, brake for a soft landing. Landed on a roof, F lets you rappel down. The sea and thin ice are unforgiving.

Wind. By parachute, hang glider and plane, an arrow at the end of the heading strip shows where the wind is pushing you; it turns red when the weather forbids free flight.

Cable car and belfry. F to board the cabin; the mouse turns your head. In the belfry, walk to the openings; C crouches behind the parapet.

8.8With a controller

Left stick · right stickMove · look.
AJump, stand up.
BMoving: speed tuck; standing still: go down one position.
XInteract.
Y · D-pad ← →Next weapon · previous, next weapon.
D-pad ↑ · D-pad ↓Fire mode · knife strike (with binoculars: zoom).
Left · right triggerAim · fire.
Left · right bumperGrenade · binoculars.
Left · right stick clickFast time · campfire.
View (Select) · Menu (Start)Map · pause.

8.9In the editor

Ctrl+ZUndo the last edit (Cmd on Mac).
Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+YRedo.
EnterClose a patrol's round.
Delete BackspaceRemove the selected item.
EscAbandon the round in progress, or deselect.

Credits

Guérilla — Vetrarhríð, Studio Thelba. A free remake of Midwinter (Mike Singleton, 1989); original island, characters and story.

Weapon and arm modelling: Baptiste Barbe, 3D artist. Characters and dogs: Quaternius (CC0). Cars: Kenney (CC0). Textures: Poly Haven and ambientCG (CC0). Real-world maps: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), Terrain Tiles elevation. Made with Unity and Blender.

Illustrations: in-game captures (Unity beta). This booklet describes beta 0.10.2; some details may change before release.
